templates.pattern: Vigenère cipher, key=CAT. Decode: [CIPHER]
templates.explanation: Vigenère: shift each cipher letter back by key letter position. CAT=C(2),A(0),T(19). EOXH-CAT=BLUE

templates.pattern: Rail fence cipher, [N] rails. Decode: [CIPHER]
templates.explanation: Rail fence: write zigzag across N rails, read rows. Reverse to decode.

templates.pattern: Columnar transposition, key order=[ORDER]. Decode: [CIPHER]
templates.explanation: Columnar transposition: write text in rows, read by column order. Reverse to decode.

templates.pattern: Hill cipher: matrix [[2,1],[1,1]], vector [[X],[Y]] mod 26. Result?
templates.explanation: Hill cipher: multiply matrix row by vector. Top row [2,1]: result = (2*X + Y) mod 26

templates.pattern: RSA-like: N=[P]×[Q], e=[E], message=[M]. Cipher = M^E mod N?
templates.explanation: Simplified RSA: C = M^E mod N where N=P×Q. Cipher = [M]^[E] mod ([P]×[Q]) = [RESULT]

templates.pattern: Gronsfeld cipher, key=[KEY_NUM]. Decode: [CIPHER]
templates.explanation: Gronsfeld: like Vigenère but key is digits. Shift each cipher letter back by digit. BDF-123=ACE

templates.pattern: Permutation cipher, perm=[P1][P2][P3][P4]. ABCD becomes?
templates.explanation: Permutation: rearrange letters by position mapping. 3142 means: pos1→3rd, pos2→1st, pos3→4th, pos4→2nd

templates.pattern: Beaufort cipher, key=A. Decode: [CIPHER]
templates.explanation: Beaufort with key=A: C = (Key - Plain) mod 26. Key=A means shift=0, so cipher = plain unchanged.

templates.pattern: Homophonic substitution: A=[X]. Which letter does code [X] represent?
templates.explanation: Homophonic: multiple codes map to same letter. 1,26,51 all = A. 2,27,52 all = B.

templates.pattern: Skip transposition: Write [TEXT] in [R] rows, read every [S]th. Result?
templates.explanation: Write text in R rows, read taking every Sth letter. HELLO in 2 rows: HLO/EL → skip read = HLOEL

templates.pattern: Morse ambiguity: [MORSE] could represent how many different letters?
templates.explanation: Standard Morse: each pattern = exactly 1 letter. .-=A, ..=I, ---=O, .--=W

templates.pattern: VIC cipher complexity: Step [STEP] of 10. How complex is this step?
templates.explanation: VIC cipher has 10 progressive steps. Steps 1-2=very low, 3-4=low, 5-6=medium, 7-8=high, 9-10=very high

templates.pattern: Fractal cipher: [N] iterations from seed. Pattern size grows to?
templates.explanation: Fractal cipher: each iteration triples the pattern size. After N iterations = 3^N characters

templates.pattern: Polybius square: Row [R], Col [C]. In 5x5 grid A-Z (no Q), which letter?
templates.explanation: 5x5 Polybius: Row1=ABCDE, Row2=FGHIJ, Row3=KLMNO, Row4=PRSTU, Row5=VWXYZ (no Q)

templates.pattern: Caesar cipher shift +[N]. Encode: [WORD]
templates.explanation: Caesar: shift each letter forward by N. HELLO+3=KHOOR. HELLO+13=URYYB (ROT13)

templates.pattern: Affine cipher: a=[A], b=[B]. Encode letter [L] (0-25). Result?
templates.explanation: Affine cipher: C = (a×L + b) mod 26. With a=[A], b=[B], L=[L]: ([A]×[L]+[B]) mod 26 = [RESULT]

templates.pattern: Vigenère with key=KEY. Encode letter A(=0) with key letter [K](=?). Result?
templates.explanation: Vigenère: encode A(0) with key letter. K=10, so A+10=K. E=4, so A+4=E. Y=24, so A+24=Y

templates.pattern: XOR stream cipher: key byte=[KB], plain byte=[PB]. Cipher byte?
templates.explanation: XOR stream: C = Key XOR Plain. [KB] XOR [PB] = [RESULT]. XOR is reversible: same operation decodes.

templates.pattern: Transposition: HELLO written in [R] rows of [C] cols. Read column [COL]?
templates.explanation: HELLO in 2 rows of 3 cols: H E L / L O *. Col1=HL, Col2=EO, Col3=LL

templates.pattern: Double transposition: first key=[K1], second key=[K2]. Security level?
templates.explanation: Double transposition: applying two columnar transpositions. Longer keys = higher security.

templates.pattern: One-time pad: key=[KB], plain=[PB]. XOR cipher byte?
templates.explanation: One-time pad: perfectly secure if key is random and used once. C = K XOR P = [KB] XOR [PB] = [RESULT]

templates.pattern: Substitution cipher strength: alphabet size [N]. How many possible keys?
templates.explanation: Simple substitution: N! possible keys. 2!=2, 3!=6, 4!=24, 26!=4×10^26 (astronomical)

templates.pattern: Running key cipher vs Vigenère: key length [KL] vs message length [ML]. More secure?
templates.explanation: Running key: key as long as message = no repeating pattern. KL≥ML means running key wins.

templates.pattern: Index of coincidence: random text ≈ [R], English ≈ [E]. Value [V] suggests?
templates.explanation: IC near 0.038=random cipher, 0.065=natural English. Values between suggest poly-alphabetic cipher.

templates.pattern: Kasiski test: repeated sequence found at positions [P1] and [P2]. Likely key length?
templates.explanation: Kasiski: distance between repeated sequences = likely multiple of key length. Distance = [P2]-[P1] = [RESULT]
